name: Saparua
confidence_why: Van Hoëvell 1877 and Stresemann 1927 both place Saparua stress on the penultimate syllable of the suffixed word (hulánno 'moon', palá-e 'wish', tomá-lo 'support'), and the only modern phonology, Erniati 2017 on the Sirisori dialect, reports that stress is present but not contrastive without stating its position, so the rule rests on few and old descriptions but nothing read contradicts it.

catalog_quote: [Stresemann 1927: 174] Das Ur-Ambon betonte alle mehr als einsilbigen Wörter auf der Pänultima des Grundwortes. Einsilbige Suffixe, welcher Art auch, übten auf die Lage des Tones keinen Einfluß aus. [175] Eine vierte Gruppe hat den Ton gleichfalls nach dem Wortende zu gerückt, jedoch nur, weil sich dem Stützvokal noch ein weiteres einsilbiges Suffix anheftete. Hierher gehören die Sprachen von Amahei, Nusalaut und Saparua. [176] Dagegen rückt der Akzent bei Hinzutritt dieses Suffixes im Saparua, Nusalaut, Amahei, Paulohi, dem östlichen Sapalewa-Dialekt, den Wemale-Dialekten sowie im Sepa auf die nunmehrige Pänultima. wünschen Spr., N. palá-e [177] Die Nominalendung -lo, welche sich im Amahei, Saparua und Nusalaut jedem Präfix-Substantivum anheftet, beeinflußt die Lage des Akzentes nicht: Feuer SA. ápu(y) > Am. háu-ro, Spr., N. háu-lo ... new_statements.quote: Berdasarkan data di atas, dalam bahasa Sirisori tidak terdapat adanya tekanan, nada, dan panjang pendeknya bunyi yang dapat mengubah arti suatu kata. Oleh karena itu, dapat dikatakan bahwa tekanan, nada, dan panjang pendeknya bunyi tidak terdapat dalam fonem bahasa Sirisori. [p. 76] ... Berdasarkan data, walaupun dalam bahasa Sirisori terdapat unsur-unsur suprasegmental berupa tekanan, nada, dan durasi, akan tetapi tidak terdapat unsur suprasegmental yang distingtif, atau yang membedakan makna. Oleh karena itu, dapat disimpulkan bahwa dalam bahasa Sirisori tidak terdapat fonem suprasegmental. [pp. 82-83]
new_statements.translation: Based on the data above, in the Sirisori language there is no stress, pitch or length of sounds that can change the meaning of a word. Therefore it can be said that stress, pitch and length are not among the phonemes of Sirisori. ... Based on the data, although Sirisori has suprasegmental elements in the form of stress, pitch and duration, there is no distinctive suprasegmental element, i.e. none that distinguishes meaning. Therefore it can be concluded that Sirisori has no suprasegmental phonemes.
new_statements.citation: Erniati. 2017. Fonologi Bahasa Sirisori. Ambon: Kantor Bahasa Maluku, Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa, Kementerian Pendidikan dan Kebudayaan. ISBN 978-602-60859-5-5.

new_statements.rule_in_words: The only descriptive source states that stress (tekanan) exists phonetically but is not contrastive (no minimal pairs; no suprasegmental phonemes). It gives NO rule for where word stress falls; the placement question is unanswered. (Erniati 2016, same author and village, notes vowel allophones in 'open syllables that receive stress' but likewise states no position.)
new_statements.exceptions: None for stress. The section lists words with a long-pronounced open or closed syllable in initial, medial or final position (e.g. /raalio/ 'monkey', /hahid:ɔ/ 'fish-hook', /paid:ɔ/ 'mat') as non-contrastive length.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level; elicited citation forms (Swadesh and thematic wordlists) from native speakers in Negeri Sirisori Islam, Kecamatan Saparua; describes the Sirisori variety only.
new_statements.identity_note: Erniati 2017 (and Erniati 2016) describe the variety of Negeri Sirisori Islam on Saparua Island, i.e. the Siri-Sori dialect (Glottolog siri1271) of Saparua [sapa1251, spr]. Erniati notes (p. 3) that the Badan Bahasa language-mapping team classified 'bahasa Sirisori' lexicostatistically as a dialect of 'bahasa Asilulu' (51-80% cognacy), a classification that differs from Glottolog/Collins; she uses the name 'bahasa Sirisori'. Collins 1983 fn. 6 lists Sirisori Islam, Iha and Kulur (Saparua), Iha-Kulur (west Seram) and Tumalehu, Hualoi, Latu (Elpaputi Bay) as the surviving communities of the Saparua language.

readall_conflicts: The standing tension in the record is between the catalog's penultimate rule and Erniati 2017 (Sirisori Islam), which says stress, tone and length do not change word meaning in Sirisori ('tidak terdapat dalam fonem bahasa Sirisori', p. 76). That is a statement about contrastiveness, not placement, and it is compatible with a fixed penultimate stress; Erniati 2016 (Totobuang 4(1), pp. 34-35, held by the project in this folder) even refers to allophones 'pada suku terbuka yang mendapat tekanan', so stress exists phonetically. 13-14, for the Ambonese dialects including Saparua ('Omtrent den klemtoon is op te merken, dat deze.. in den regel valt op de voorlaatste lettergreep'; Saparua example p. 12 hulánno 'moon'), and Stresemann 1927, § 177, pp. 175-176, who says Saparua (with Nusalaut and Amahei) moved the accent to the new penultimate of the suffixed word ('wünschen Spr., N. palá-e'; 'stützen Spr., N. tomá-lo'). So the best-supported reading remains penultimate stress counted on the suffixed word, with a caveat that the only modern description (Erniati) treats it as non-phonemic.
